(Lakeville, Minnesota) | college = [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]] (2014–2018) | draft_year = 2018 | career_start = 2018 | years1 = {{nbay|2018|full=y}} | team1 = [[Charlotte Hornets]] | years2 = 2018–2019 | team2 = → [[Greensboro Swarm]] | years3 = 2019–2020 | team3 = [[Canton Charge]] | years4 = {{nbay|2019|end}} | team4 = [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] | years5 = 2020–2021 | team5 = [[Afyon Belediye S.K.|Afyon Belediye]] | years6 = 2021–2023 | team6 = [[Derthona Basket|Derthona]] | years7 = 2024–2025 | team7 = [[Universo Treviso Basket|Treviso]] | years8 = 2025–2026 | team8 = [[Promitheas Patras B.C.|Promitheas Patras]] | years9 = 2026–present | team9 = Treviso | highlights = * [[Big East Conference|Big East]] [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Sixth Man of the Year|Sixth Man of the Year]] (2016) }} '''Jonathan Paul Macura''' (born June 5, 1995) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Universo Treviso Basket|Treviso]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]]. He played college basketball for [[Xavier University]]. ==High school career== Macura attended [[Lakeville North High School]] in [[Lakeville, Minnesota]].{{cite web|title=#50 J.P. Macura|url=http://goxavier.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=2108|website=GoXavier.com|accessdate=April 10, 2018}} At the school, Macura won one [[MSHSL]] state title. He scored 1,811 points in his career, a school record. In his senior season, he averaged 32.2 points and 6.5 rebounds per game. Macura led his team to victory in the 2014 4A state tournament over [[Hopkins High School]], and hit a buzzer-beating three-pointer to win the semifinal game over [[Cretin-Derham Hall High School]]. He received scholarship offers from [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]] and [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] but committed to Xavier to compete in the [[Big East Conference]].{{cite news|last=Stubbs|first=Roman|title=J.P. Macura is the Grayson Allen of Big East basketball|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/jp-macura-is-the-grayson-allen-of-big-east-basketball/2018/02/08/39caaa02-079a-11e8-8777-2a059f168dd2_story.html|accessdate=April 15, 2018|work=[[Washington Post]]|date=February 9, 2018}} ==College career== Macura made his first two collegiate starts at [[2014–15 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] on January 14, 2015, and at [[2014–15 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Marquette]] on January 17. He recorded back-to-back double-figure-scoring games for the first time in his Xavier career with an 11-point game at Marquette on February 10 and a 10-point game in a win over [[2014–15 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]] on February 7. On March 13 against [[2014–15 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]], Macura scored eight points in just seven minutes of action, including going 2-of-2 from three-point territory, before being forced out of the game with an ankle injury. He was forced to sit out the [[Big East Conference]] championship game, but returned for the [[2014–15 Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball team|Ole Miss]] game on March 19 and hit two 3-pointers. In [[2014–15 Xavier Musketeers men's basketball team|2014–15]], he was seventh on the team in scoring with 5.4 points per game, and third on the team in steals with 26 (0.7 steals per game) in just 13.2 minutes per game. Macura was voted the 2015–16 [[Big East Conference]] [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Sixth Man of the Year|Sixth Man of the Year]] award winner by the Big East coaches in 2016. He provided high energy with 9.4 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game on the season.{{cite news|last=Grasha|first=Kevin|title=Xavier player who pulled down pants pleads guilty|url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/news/2016/05/24/xavier-player-who-pulled-down-pants-pleads-guilty/84851526/|accessdate=April 15, 2018|work=[[Cincinnati Enquirer]]|date=May 24, 2016}} In the last 15 games of the season, he averaged 10.6 points per game on 48.6 percent shooting, including 41.2 percent from 3-point territory. Macura scored in double figures in nine of the last 15 games and 16 for the season, including a team-high-tying 19 points to go with three steals in the win over [[2015–16 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] on February 24, 2016. He hit 80.7 percent from the free-throw line, although he did not have enough attempts to be ranked in the Big East Conference (he would have been 10th). Macura had a season-high 20-point effort in 31 minutes of action versus [[2015–16 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Marquette]] on February 6 that included two clutch 3-pointers in the final four minutes. In March 2016, Macura pulled down his pants and was caught with a fake ID in a Cincinnati bar. He was charged with disorderly conduct. On November 18, Macura scored a career-high 28 points in an 83–77 win over [[2016–17 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]].{{cite news|title=No. 11 Xavier defeats Clemson 83-77 in Tire Pros tournament|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400926407|access-date=April 17, 2018|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=November 18, 2016}} He averaged 14.4 points per game as a junior.{{cite news|last=Braziller|first=Zach|title=Meet the Xavier star who loves being the bad guy|url=https://nypost.com/2018/03/07/meet-the-xavier-star-who-loves-being-the-bad-guy/|accessdate=April 15, 2018|work=[[New York Post]]|date=March 7, 2018}} As a senior, Macura received the nickname "Dennis the Menace" due to taunting opposing players. Whenever he received a crude tweet, he replied "Thank you, God Bless." He had 27 points against [[2017–18 Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball team|Seton Hall]] on January 20. Macura averaged 12.9 points per game on a 29–6 team that earned Xavier's first no. 1 seed in the NCAA tournament. He finished his career with 1,491 points.{{cite web|title=Trevon Bluiett and J.P. Macura Selected For Inaugural 3-on-3 National Championship|url=http://goxavier.com/news/2018/3/22/mens-basketball-trevon-bluiett-and-j-pmacura-selected-for-inaugural-3x3u-national-championship.aspx|website=[[Xavier Musketeers]]|accessdate=April 15, 2018}} ==Professional career== ===Charlotte Hornets/Greensboro Swarm (2018–2019)=== After going undrafted in the [[2018 NBA draft]], Macura signed a two-way contract with the [[Charlotte Hornets]], splitting time between the Hornets and their [[G League]] affiliate the [[Greensboro Swarm]].{{cite web |last=Wash |first=Quinton |date=July 2, 2018 |title=Hornets Sign J.P. Macura To A Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/hornets-sign-jp-macura-two-way-contract |accessdate=July 2, 2018 |website=NBA.com}} In his first game with the Swarm, he scored 27 points in a 114–98 win against the [[Wisconsin Herd]].{{cite news |last=Clark |first=Dave |title=J.P. Macura scores 27 in NBA G-League debut for Greensboro Swarm |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/xavier/2018/11/03/j-p-macura-scores-27-nba-g-league-debut-greensboro-swarm/1870403002/ |accessdate=November 4, 2018 |work=[[Cincinnati Enquirer]] |date=November 3, 2018}} Macura made his NBA debut on January 2, 2019, in a 122–84 blowout loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]], recording 4 points, 2 rebounds, and 2 assists in 13 minutes of action.{{Cite web|url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/xavier/2019/01/03/j-p-macura-scores-first-nba-basket-charlotte-hornets-loss/2470150002/|title=Watch: J.P. Macura scores first NBA basket for Charlotte Hornets against Dallas Mavericks}} ===Canton Charge (2019–2020)=== Macura signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in July 2019.{{cite news |last=Clark |first=Dave |title=J.P. Macura, Cleveland Cavaliers agree to partially guaranteed deal, per reports |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/xavier/2019/07/25/jp-macura-cleveland-cavs-reach-partially-guaranteed-deal-per-reports/1833570001/ |accessdate=26 October 2019 |work=[[Cincinnati Enquirer]] |date=July 25, 2019 |language=en}} He was released along with [[Sindarius Thornwell]], [[Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot]] and [[Daniel Hamilton (basketball)|Daniel Hamilton]] on October 15, 2019. He later signed with the Cavaliers G League affiliate [[Canton Charge]].{{cite news |last=Fedor |first=Chris |title=Cleveland Cavaliers release Sindarius Thornwell, Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot, J.P. Macura and Daniel Hamilton, sources say |url=https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/2019/10/cleveland-cavaliers-release-sindarius-thornwell-timothe-luwawu-cabarrot-jp-macura-and-daniel-hamilton-sources-say.html |accessdate=26 October 2019 |work=Cleveland.com |date=16 October 2019 |language=en}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2020)=== On February 9, 2020, the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] announced that they had signed Macura to a 10-day contract.{{cite web |last=Gold |first=Matthew |date=February 9, 2020 |title=Cavaliers Sign J.P. Macura And Malik Newman To 10-Day Contracts |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/macura-newman-contracts-200209 |accessdate=February 9, 2020 |website=NBA.com}} Macura appeared in one game for the Cavaliers before his contract expired. ===Afyon Belediye (2020–2021)=== On September 8, 2020, he has signed with [[Afyon Belediye S.K.|Afyon Belediye]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/643750/J.P.-Macura-joins-Afyon|title=J.P. Macura joins Afyon|last=|first=|date=September 8, 2020|website=|publisher=Eurobasket|language=En|access-date=September 8, 2020}} He averaged 12.9 points, 3.9 rebounds, 1.7 assists and 1.7 steals per game. ===Derthona Basket (2021–2023)=== On July 24, 2021, Macura signed with [[Derthona Basket]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]].{{cite news |last=Skerletic |first=Dario |date=July 24, 2021 |title=J.P. Macura signs with Bertram Derthona |website=Sportando |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/j-p-macura-signs-with-bertram-derthona/ |access-date=July 24, 2021}} ===Treviso Basket (2024–2025)=== On August 5, 2024, he signed with [[Universo Treviso Basket|Treviso Basket]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Italy/news/885688/JP-Macura-is-a-newcomer-at-Treviso|title=JP Macura is a newcomer at Treviso|last=|first=|date=August 5, 2024|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=February 10, 2025}} ===Promitheas Patras (2025–2026)=== On August 7, 2025, Macura signed with Greek club [[Promitheas Patras B.C.|Promitheas]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Greece/news/948685/Promitheas-ink-JP-Macura-ex-Treviso|title=Promitheas ink JP Macura, ex Treviso|last=|first=|date=August 7, 2025|website=|publisher=Eurobasket|language=En|access-date=October 11, 2025}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2018}} | style="text-align;left;"| [[2018–19 Charlotte Hornets season|Charlotte]] | '''2''' || 0 || '''8.5''' || '''.333''' || .000 || -
